commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Do not always translate 一応 as “for now.” Depending on the situation, it often means “just in case,” “technically,” or “at least to a basic degree.” Pay attention to what the speaker is trying to accomplish rather than forcing one English translation.

keywords.meaning: for now; just in case; technically
keywords.nuance: 一応 often shows that something has been done to a basic or acceptable extent, but perhaps not perfectly or with full confidence. It can also describe doing something as a precaution.
keywords.example: 一応、確認しておきます。

questions.prompt: 宿題は一応終わりました。
questions.hint: The homework is finished to a basic degree, though the speaker may not feel completely satisfied with it.
questions.answer: I finished my homework, more or less. / My homework is technically finished.

questions.prompt: 雨が降るかもしれないので、一応傘を持っていきます。
questions.hint: Here, 一応 describes taking a precaution.
questions.answer: It might rain, so I’ll bring an umbrella just in case.

questions.prompt: 一応、日本語を話せます。
questions.hint: The speaker qualifies the claim and avoids sounding overly confident.
questions.answer: Technically, I can speak Japanese. / I can speak some Japanese, at least.

questions.prompt: 一応、彼にも連絡しておいたほうがいいと思います。
questions.hint: The speaker suggests doing something as a precaution.
questions.answer: I think we should contact him too, just in case.
